content: 1. Symptoms or signs of pregnancy should be evaluated, and the following criteria must be met to rule out pregnancy: The individual is within 7 days of the start of their last normal menstrual period. The individual has not engaged in sexual intercourse since the beginning of their last normal menstrual period. The individual has been consistently and correctly using a reliable method of contraception. The individual is within 7 days following a spontaneous or induced abortion. The individual is within 4 weeks postpartum. The individual is exclusively or predominantly breastfeeding, is amenorrheic, and is less than 6 months postpartum. 2. Timing for the initiation of copper intrauterine devices (Cu-IUDs): A Cu-IUD can be inserted at any time if it is reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant. A Cu-IUD can also be inserted within 5 days of the first act of unprotected sexual intercourse as an emergency contraceptive. If the day of ovulation can be estimated, the Cu-IUD may be inserted more than 5 days after unprotected intercourse, provided the insertion does not occur more than 5 days after ovulation. 3. No additional contraceptive protection is required after the insertion of a Cu-IUD. 4. Special considerations for amenorrheic individuals (not postpartum): A Cu-IUD can be inserted at any time if it is reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant. No additional contraceptive protection is needed after insertion. 5. Switching from another contraceptive method: A Cu-IUD can be inserted immediately if it is reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant. Waiting for the next menstrual cycle is unnecessary. No additional contraceptive protection is required after insertion. 6. In cases where the healthcare provider cannot be reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant, another contraceptive method should be provided until pregnancy can be ruled out and the Cu-IUD can be safely inserted. 7. A systematic review of eight studies found that the timing of Cu-IUD insertion in relation to the menstrual cycle in non-postpartum individuals had minimal impact on long-term outcomes (such as continuation rates, removal rates, expulsion rates, or pregnancy rates) or short-term outcomes (such as pain, bleeding, or immediate expulsion at the time of insertion). 8. Timing for the initiation of levonorgestrel intrauterine devices (LNG-IUDs): An LNG-IUD can be inserted at any time if it is reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant. 9. Back-up contraception for LNG-IUDs: If the LNG-IUD is inserted within the first 7 days of menstrual bleeding, no additional contraceptive protection is needed. If the LNG-IUD is inserted more than 7 days after the start of menstrual bleeding, the individual should abstain from sexual intercourse or use additional contraceptive protection for the next 7 days. 10. Special considerations for amenorrheic individuals (not postpartum): An LNG-IUD can be inserted at any time if it is reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant. The individual should abstain from sexual intercourse or use additional contraceptive protection for the next 7 days after insertion. 11. Postpartum considerations (including after cesarean delivery): An LNG-IUD can be inserted immediately if it is reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant. 12. Switching from another contraceptive method: An LNG-IUD can be inserted immediately if it is reasonably certain that the individual is not pregnant. Waiting for the next menstrual cycle is unnecessary.
